Subject: Northbridge Bank - questions on Redwood Private observability (dashboards/alerts) + SIEM export + air-gapped packaging

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. As discussed, we’re reviewing Redwood Private for a VPC deployment first, with a follow-on on-prem (air-gapped) environment.

Could you confirm the following for the “minimum supported” observability pack?

1) Dashboards/alerts
- Which dashboards ship by default? (Runtime, control plane, GPU, queueing/backpressure, etc.)
- Do the alert rules map to SLO burn (latency/availability), or are they mostly resource-based thresholds?
- How are alert severities handled (page vs ticket)?

2) Logs + SIEM export
- What components are covered (gateway/control plane/runtime)?
- Is the logging structured (JSON)? Do you log request/response bodies?
- Supported sinks: Splunk HEC is our preference; ELK/OpenSearch also used in some envs. Do you support both?
- Any OTLP support for logs/metrics/traces? (We run an OTEL Collector standard.)

3) Air-gapped / offline packaging (on-prem)
- Do you provide a single offline bundle with all container images + dashboards/rules/configs?
- Do we need to mirror images into our own registry? How is integrity verified (checksums/signing)?
- Upgrade/rollback: what breaks commonly (metric renames, dashboard IDs, etc.)?

If it’s easier, a short write-up is fine. We can review internally and consolidate follow-ups.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Director, Platform Observability
Northbridge Bank

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Ravi Iyer <ravi.iyer@northbridgebank.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 20, 2025 at 12:03 PM ET
Subject: Re: Northbridge Bank - questions on Redwood Private observability (dashboards/alerts) + SIEM export + air-gapped packaging

Hi Alyssa (hi Ravi),

Absolutely — below is the most concrete view of what we support today for Private installs and what we’re packaging as the “minimum supported” baseline.

1) Dashboards + alerts (minimum pack)

Dashboards that ship (Grafana JSON, versioned with the release):
- Runtime Overview: request rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, batching behavior, queue depth/backpressure, KV cache hit rate/pressure, GPU utilization & memory, per-pod health.
- Control Plane Health: API gateway, routing/policy engine, auth/RBAC integration points, installer/upgrade controller health, config propagation delays.
- Infra / Cluster: CPU/mem pressure, pod restarts, OOM kills, PVC/storage pressure for Prometheus/Grafana (when deployed in-cluster), scrape health.

Alerts:
- We include both SLO-oriented alerts (latency + availability burn) and “symptom” alerts (scrape failures, restart loops, resource saturation).
- SLO burn: we follow a standard multi-window multi-burn approach (fast burn pages, slow burn tickets) for API availability and request latency. The intent is to catch customer impact early without paging on normal variance.
- Resource alerts: GPU saturation, GPU memory pressure, container OOMKilled, repeated restarts, disk almost full (Prometheus/Grafana storage), and backlog/queue growth when the runtime cannot keep up.

Severities / page vs ticket:
- The pack ships with severities encoded (critical/high/medium) in alert labels + annotations.
- Default behavior is “customer chooses routing.” Many customers wire only critical/high to paging and keep medium as ticket/Slack.
- We include runbook links in alert annotations (what to check first / likely causes / known fixes).

2) Logs + SIEM export

Coverage:
- Control plane services, API gateway, routing/policy engine, serving runtime pods, and installer/upgrade controller.

Format & sensitive content:
- Logs are structured JSON by default.
- We do NOT log request/response bodies by default. Operational logs focus on metadata (request_id, component, status, latency, selected model/route at an aggregate-safe level) and infrastructure events.
- Redaction: secrets/credentials are never intended to be logged; guidance is included for customer-side forwarders to drop/replace specific fields if desired.

Supported sinks (what we’ve tested/expect to support in Private environments):
- Splunk HEC: supported configuration (token auth + TLS; customer provides endpoint and token).
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch: supported configuration.
- Loki: supported configuration (common for customers running Grafana stack).
- OTLP: on the roadmap for broader Private parity; today most Private customers use Splunk/ELK/Loki sinks. If OTLP is a hard requirement for GA, we can talk about timing/commitment (happy to align on your collector expectations).

Traces:
- Minimum pack is metrics+logs first; traces are “best effort” depending on the environment and what you’re running in-cluster. If you already standardize on OTEL Collector, we can walk through options.

3) Air-gapped / offline packaging

Offline bundle contents:
- Yes: for on-prem/air-gapped we provide an offline artifact bundle that includes required container images (for the observability components we ship), plus the versioned dashboards, Prometheus alert rules/recording rules, and default log collector configuration.

Image mirroring + integrity:
- Yes: you mirror images into your own registry.
- We provide an image list and checksums for the offline bundle artifacts; in practice customers validate the bundle and then mirror/pin to their internal registry.

Upgrade/rollback:
- We treat metric names/labels as a compatibility surface. When we must change names/labels, we provide a migration note and keep backwards-compatibility where feasible via recording rules.
- The most common “break” we see in the field is Grafana datasources/auth or dashboards not being imported after upgrades (usually permissions or sidecar config). We have a documented post-upgrade validation checklist to catch this quickly.

I’m attaching a short draft architecture write-up that illustrates the minimum pack components and the log export paths we see most commonly.

Attachment(s):
- Redwood-Private-Observability-Min-Pack-Architecture-Draft-v0.3.pdf (application/pdf)

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute session next week focused only on: (a) Splunk HEC wiring and (b) what the offline bundle would look like in your on-prem change-control process.

Best,
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Ravi,

Good questions — answers inline.

1) Logs (identifiers, audit vs ops)
- Identifiers: operational logs can include a request_id and a tenant identifier in a privacy-safe form. For Private deployments we recommend (and in many cases default to) a hashed/opaque tenant ID rather than a raw customer/user identifier.
- We do not require logging end-user identifiers. If your deployment would pass anything user-specific through headers, we recommend dropping those headers at the gateway and/or configuring the log collector to exclude them.
- Audit vs operational: yes, there is a separation conceptually. Auth/config/admin actions should be captured in audit logs (who changed routing policy, who updated config, installer actions), while operational logs cover runtime health and request processing. We can walk through the exact event types you expect in an audit trail.

2) Prometheus/Grafana requirement
- Prometheus + Grafana are the assumed reference stack for the minimum pack dashboards/alerts as shipped (Grafana dashboards + Prometheus rules).
- That said, the metrics are standard Prometheus-format. Many customers scrape with their own Prometheus-compatible backend; the key is ensuring the same metric names/labels and recording rules exist so dashboards/alerts render/behave as expected.
- If you want to use your managed backend but still load our dashboards, we typically just point Grafana at your backend as the datasource.

Configs/examples
- Attaching a small zip with example Helm values snippets for Splunk HEC, Loki, and a generic OTEL Collector endpoint placeholder (note: OTLP export is not our “most battle-tested” path in Private yet, but I included the shape of config customers usually ask for).

Attachment(s):
- private-observability-values-examples-splunk-loki-otel.zip (application/zip)

If you can share (even high level) whether your on-prem environment requires FIPS mode, strict egress deny, or customer-managed CA bundles, I can tailor the recommended packaging/validation checklist for your change-control.

Best,
Markus
